The Extended Marching Cubes Lookup Table is a surface extraction method that eliminates degenerate, zero-area triangles by distinguishing scalar values equal to the isovalue from those strictly greater than it [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the Extended Marching Cubes algorithm uses a lookup table that differentiates scalar values equal to the isovalue ('=') from those strictly greater than the isovalue ('+'). It further explains that standard Marching Cubes treats '=' and '+' identically, which leads to degenerate, zero-area triangles. The extended method avoids this by using three labels ('+', '-', '=') and a larger lookup table (3^8 entries), thereby eliminating these degenerate cases.

The work addresses the limitation of standard Marching Cubes, which can produce degenerate triangles when scalar values equal the isovalue [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that standard Marching Cubes treats scalar values equal to the isovalue ('=') and scalar values greater than the isovalue ('+') identically. This indistinguishability causes the algorithm to position multiple isosurface vertices at the same grid vertex, resulting in degenerate triangles. The evidence further confirms that the work addresses this limitation by introducing an extended lookup table that distinguishes between these cases.
